markers.label: Russian pipeline gas to Europe falls by about half

sources.name: IEA: Gas Market Lessons from the 2022–2023 Energy Crisis — Anatomy of a natural gas crisis

steps.title: 2021: Russia and Norway supply the EU
text: In 2021 the [EU](EU) imported **$109 billion** of natural gas from outside the EU. [Norway](NOR) supplied 35% and [Russia](RUS) **28%**; the [United States](USA), 8%.
Arcs show where the EU's gas came from (CEPII BACI; pipeline gas and LNG).

steps.title: 2022: the bill nearly triples
text: After [Russia](RUS) invaded Ukraine, its pipeline gas exports to Europe fell by about half in 2022, and Europe replaced them mainly with liquefied natural gas (LNG), whose imports rose by more than 60%.
Prices soared, so the [EU](EU) paid **$314 billion** for gas imports in 2022, 2.9 times as much as in 2021. Russia's share fell to 18%; [US](USA) gas brought in $37.6 billion.

stat.label: the EU's bill for gas imports in 2022, compared with 2021

steps.title: New suppliers
text: By 2024 the bill was back to **$112 billion**. The [United States](USA) supplied **17%** of the [EU](EU)'s gas imports, more than [Russia](RUS) (16%); [Norway](NOR) remained the largest at 35%.
Lines show each supplier's share of the EU's gas imports over time.

steps.title: A record deficit
text: Expensive energy turned the [EU](EU)'s trade with the rest of the world from a **$50 billion** surplus in 2021 to a **$492 billion** deficit in 2022; its energy imports rose 85% to $829 billion. By 2024 it was back to a $102 billion surplus.
[Germany](DEU)'s own surplus fell from $213 billion to $84 billion in 2022, then recovered.
